title: Checks that type TypeVars, ParamSpecs, and TypeVarTuples in stubs have names prefixed with _.
summary: Prefixing type parameters with _ avoids accidentally exposing names internal to the stub. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.245.
message_templates: Name of private `{}` must start with `_`

title: Checks for if statements with complex conditionals in stubs.
summary: Type checkers understand simple conditionals to express variations between different Python versions and platforms. However, complex tests may not be understood by a type checker, leading to incorrect inferences when they analyze your code. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.276.
message_templates: `if` test must be a simple comparison against `sys.platform` or `sys.version_info`

title: Checks for problematic sys.version_info-related conditions in stubs.
summary: Stub files support simple conditionals to test for differences in Python versions using sys.version_info. However, there are a number of common mistakes involving sys.version_info comparisons that should be avoided. For example, comparing against a string can lead to unexpected behavior. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.276.
message_templates: Unrecognized `sys.version_info` check

title: Checks for Python version comparisons in stubs that compare against patch versions (e.g., Python 3.8.3) instead of major and minor versions (e.g., Python 3.8).
summary: Stub files support simple conditionals to test for differences in Python versions and platforms. However, type checkers only understand a limited subset of these conditionals. In particular, type checkers don't support patch versions (e.g., Python 3.8.3), only major and minor versions (e.g., Python 3.8). Therefore, version checks in stubs should only use the major and minor versions. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.276.
message_templates: Version comparison must use only major and minor version

title: Checks for Python version comparisons that compare against a tuple of the wrong length.
summary: Stub files support simple conditionals to test for differences in Python versions and platforms. When comparing against sys.version_info, avoid comparing against tuples of the wrong length, which can lead to unexpected behavior. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.276.
message_templates: Version comparison must be against a length-{} tuple

title: Checks for uses of comparators other than < and >= for sys.version_info checks.
summary: All other comparators, such as >, <=, and ==, are banned. Comparing sys.version_info with == or <= has unexpected behavior and can lead to bugs. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.254.
message_templates: Use `<` or `>=` for `sys.version_info` comparisons

title: Check for unrecognized sys.platform checks.
summary: Platform checks should be simple string comparisons. Some sys.platform checks are too complex for type checkers to understand, and thus result in incorrect inferences by these tools. sys.platform checks should be simple string comparisons, like if sys.platform == "linux". Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.246.
message_templates: Unrecognized `sys.platform` check

title: Check for unrecognized platform names in sys.platform checks.
summary: If a sys.platform check compares to a platform name outside of a small set of known platforms (e.g. "linux", "win32", etc.), it's likely a typo or a platform name that is not recognized by type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.246.
message_templates: Unrecognized platform `{}`

title: Checks for pass statements in empty stub bodies.
summary: For stylistic consistency, ... should always be used rather than pass in stub files. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Empty body should contain `...`, not `pass`

title: Checks for non-empty function stub bodies.
summary: Stub files are never executed at runtime; they should be thought of as "data files" for type checkers or IDEs. Function bodies are redundant for this purpose. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Function body must contain only `...`

title: Checks for typed function arguments in stubs with complex default values.
summary: Stub (.pyi) files exist as "data files" for static analysis tools, and are not evaluated at runtime. While simple default values may be useful for some tools that consume stubs, such as IDEs, they are ignored by type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Only simple default values allowed for typed arguments

title: Checks for the presence of the pass statement in non-empty class bodies in .pyi files.
summary: The pass statement is always unnecessary in non-empty class bodies in stubs. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.260.
message_templates: Class body must not contain `pass`

title: Removes ellipses (...) in otherwise non-empty class bodies.
summary: An ellipsis in a class body is only necessary if the class body is otherwise empty. If the class body is non-empty, then the ellipsis is redundant. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.270.
message_templates: Non-empty class body must not contain `...`

title: Checks for untyped function arguments in stubs with default values that are not "simple" /// (i.e., int, float, complex, bytes, str, bool, None, ..., or simple container literals).
summary: Stub (.pyi) files exist to define type hints, and are not evaluated at runtime. As such, function arguments in stub files should not have default values, as they are ignored by type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Only simple default values allowed for arguments

title: Checks for assignments in stubs with default values that are not "simple" (i.e., int, float, complex, bytes, str, bool, None, ..., or simple container literals).
summary: Stub (.pyi) files exist to define type hints, and are not evaluated at runtime. As such, assignments in stub files should not include values, as they are ignored by type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.260.
message_templates: Only simple default values allowed for assignments

title: Checks for duplicate union members.
summary: Duplicate union members are redundant and should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.262.
message_templates: Duplicate union member `{}`

title: Checks for assignments with multiple or non-name targets in stub files.
summary: In general, stub files should be thought of as "data files" for a type checker, and are not intended to be executed. As such, it's useful to enforce that only a subset of Python syntax is allowed in a stub file, to ensure that everything in the stub is unambiguous for the type checker. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.279.
message_templates: Stubs should not contain assignments to attributes or multiple targets

title: Checks for the presence of unused private TypeVar, ParamSpec or TypeVarTuple declarations.
summary: A private TypeVar that is defined but not used is likely a mistake. It should either be used, made public, or removed to avoid confusion. A type variable is considered "private" if its name starts with an underscore. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: Private {} `{}` is never used

title: Checks for methods that use custom TypeVars in their annotations when they could use Self instead.
summary: While the semantics are often identical, using Self is more intuitive and succinct (per PEP 673) than a custom TypeVar. For example, the use of Self will typically allow for the omission of type parameters on the self and cls arguments. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.283.
message_templates: Use `Self` instead of custom TypeVar `{}`

title: Checks for quoted type annotations in stub (.pyi) files, which should be avoided.
summary: Stub files natively support forward references in all contexts, as stubs are never executed at runtime. (They should be thought of as "data files" for type checkers and IDEs.) As such, quotes are never required for type annotations in stub files, and should be omitted. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.265.
message_templates: Quoted annotations should not be included in stubs

title: Checks for the presence of docstrings in stub files.
summary: Stub files should omit docstrings, as they're intended to provide type hints, rather than documentation. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Docstrings should not be included in stubs

title: Checks for uses of collections.namedtuple in stub files.
summary: typing.NamedTuple is the "typed version" of collections.namedtuple. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Use `typing.NamedTuple` instead of `collections.namedtuple`

title: Checks for from collections.abc import Set imports that do not alias Set to AbstractSet.
summary: The Set type in collections.abc is an abstract base class for set-like types. It is easily confused with, and not equivalent to, the set builtin. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Use `from collections.abc import Set as AbstractSet` to avoid confusion with the `set` builtin

title: Checks for type alias definitions that are not annotated with typing.TypeAlias.
summary: In Python, a type alias is defined by assigning a type to a variable (e.g., Vector = listfloat). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.279.
message_templates: Use `{}.TypeAlias` for type alias, e.g., `{}: TypeAlias = {}`

title: Checks for redundant definitions of __str__ or __repr__ in stubs.
summary: Defining __str__ or __repr__ in a stub is almost always redundant, as the signatures are almost always identical to those of the default equivalent, object.__str__ and object.__repr__, respectively. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Defining `{}` in a stub is almost always redundant

title: Checks for the presence of multiple literal types in a union.
summary: Literal"foo", 42 has identical semantics to Literal"foo" | Literal42, but is clearer and more concise. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.278.
message_templates: Multiple literal members in a union. Use a single literal, e.g. `Literal[{}]`

title: Checks for __eq__ and __ne__ implementations that use typing.Any as the type annotation for their second parameter.
summary: The Python documentation recommends the use of object to "indicate that a value could be any type in a typesafe manner". Any, on the other hand, should be seen as an "escape hatch when you need to mix dynamically and statically typed code". Since using Any allows you to write highly unsafe code, you should generally only use Any when the semantics of your code would otherwise be inexpressible to the type checker. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Prefer `object` to `Any` for the second parameter to `{}`

title: Checks for the use of type comments (e.g., x = 1 # type: int).
summary: Type comments are a soft-deprecated form of type annotation. They are unsupported by some modern type checkers, including ty and Pyrefly, and are only necessary when supporting end-of-life Python versions such as 3.5 or older. They are never necessary in stub files, which are not executed at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.254.
message_templates: Don't use type comments

title: Checks for methods that are annotated with a fixed return type which should instead be returning Self.
summary: If methods that generally return self at runtime are annotated with a fixed return type, and the class is subclassed, type checkers will not be able to infer the correct return type. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: `__new__` methods usually return `self` at runtime
`{}` methods in classes like `{}` usually return `self` at runtime

title: Checks that __all__, __match_args__, and __slots__ variables are assigned to values when defined in stub files.
summary: Special variables like __all__ have the same semantics in stub files as they do in Python modules, and so should be consistent with their runtime counterparts. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: `{}` in a stub file must have a value, as it has the same semantics as `{}` at runtime

title: Checks for incorrect function signatures on __exit__ and __aexit__ methods.
summary: Improperly annotated __exit__ and __aexit__ methods can cause unexpected behavior when interacting with type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.279.
message_templates: Star-args in `{}` should be annotated with `object`
If there are no star-args, `{}` should have at least 3 non-keyword-only args (excluding `self`)
All arguments after the first four in `{}` must have a default value
All keyword-only arguments in `{}` must have a default value
The first argument in `{}` should be annotated with `object` or `type[BaseException] | None`
The second argument in `{}` should be annotated with `object` or `BaseException | None`
The third argument in `{}` should be annotated with `object` or `types.TracebackType | None`
Annotations for a three-argument `{}` overload (excluding `self`) should either be `None, None, None` or `type[BaseException], BaseException, types.TracebackType`

title: Checks for parameter annotations that contain redundant unions between builtin numeric types (e.g., int | float).
summary: The typing specification states: Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.279.
message_templates: Use `{}` instead of `{} | {}`

title: Checks for type aliases that do not use the CamelCase naming convention.
summary: It's conventional to use the CamelCase naming convention for type aliases, to distinguish them from other variables. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.265.
message_templates: Type alias `{}` should be CamelCase

title: Checks for private type alias definitions suffixed with 'T'.
summary: It's conventional to use the 'T' suffix for type variables; the use of such a suffix implies that the object is a TypeVar. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.265.
message_templates: Private type alias `{}` should not be suffixed with `T` (the `T` suffix implies that an object is a `TypeVar`)

title: Checks for the presence of the from __future__ import annotations import statement in stub files.
summary: Stub files natively support forward references in all contexts, as stubs are never executed at runtime. (They should be thought of as "data files" for type checkers.) As such, the from __future__ import annotations import statement has no effect and should be omitted. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.273.
message_templates: `from __future__ import annotations` has no effect in stub files, since type checkers automatically treat stubs as having those semantics

title: Checks for __iter__ methods in stubs that return IterableT instead of an IteratorT.
summary: __iter__ methods should always should return an Iterator of some kind, not an Iterable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: `__aiter__` methods should return an `AsyncIterator`, not an `AsyncIterable`
`__iter__` methods should return an `Iterator`, not an `Iterable`

title: Checks for the presence of unused private typing.Protocol definitions.
summary: A private typing.Protocol that is defined but not used is likely a mistake. It should either be used, made public, or removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: Private protocol `{}` is never used

title: Checks for the presence of unused private type aliases.
summary: A private type alias that is defined but not used is likely a mistake. It should either be used, made public, or removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: Private TypeAlias `{}` is never used

title: Checks for functions in stub (.pyi) files that contain multiple statements.
summary: Stub files are never executed, and are only intended to define type hints. As such, functions in stub files should not contain functional code, and should instead contain only a single statement (e.g., ...). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Function body must contain exactly one statement

title: Checks for the presence of unused private typing.TypedDict definitions.
summary: A private typing.TypedDict that is defined but not used is likely a mistake. It should either be used, made public, or removed to avoid confusion. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: Private TypedDict `{}` is never used

title: Checks for uses of typing.NoReturn (and typing_extensions.NoReturn) for parameter annotations.
summary: Prefer Never over NoReturn for parameter annotations. Never has a clearer name in these contexts, since it makes little sense to talk about a parameter annotation "not returning". Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.272.
message_templates: Prefer `{}.Never` over `NoReturn` for argument annotations

title: Checks for redundant unions between a Literal and a builtin supertype of that Literal.
summary: Using a Literal type in a union with its builtin supertype is redundant, as the supertype will be strictly more general than the Literal type. For example, Literal"A" | str is equivalent to str, and Literal1 | int is equivalent to int, as str and int are the supertypes of "A" and 1 respectively. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.283.
message_templates: `Literal[{}]` is redundant in a union with `{}`
`Literal` is redundant in a union with `{}`

title: Checks for unannotated assignments in stub (.pyi) files.
summary: Stub files exist to provide type hints, and are never executed. As such, all assignments in stub files should be annotated with a type. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.269.
message_templates: Need type annotation for `{}`

title: Checks for the use of string and bytes literals longer than 50 characters in stub (.pyi) files.
summary: If a function or variable has a default value where the string or bytes representation is greater than 50 characters long, it is likely to be an implementation detail or a constant that varies depending on the system you're running on. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: String and bytes literals longer than 50 characters are not permitted

title: Checks for numeric literals with a string representation longer than ten characters.
summary: If a function has a default value where the literal representation is greater than 10 characters, the value is likely to be an implementation detail or a constant that varies depending on the system you're running on. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.271.
message_templates: Numeric literals with a string representation longer than ten characters are not permitted

title: Checks for the presence of multiple types in a union.
summary: typeT | S has identical semantics to typeT | typeS in a type annotation, but is cleaner and more concise. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.283.
message_templates: Multiple `type` members in a union. Combine them into one, e.g., `type[{}]`.

title: Checks that append, extend and remove methods are not called on __all__.
summary: Different type checkers have varying levels of support for calling these methods on __all__. Instead, use the += operator to add items to __all__, which is known to be supported by all major type checkers. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: Calling `.{}()` on `__all__` may not be supported by all type checkers (use `+=` instead)

title: Checks for uses of typing.ByteString or collections.abc.ByteString.
summary: ByteString has been deprecated since Python 3.9 and will be removed in Python 3.17. The Python documentation recommends using either collections.abc.Buffer (or the typing_extensions backport on Python <3.12) or a union like bytes | bytearray | memoryview instead. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.6.0.
message_templates: Do not use `{}.ByteString`, which has unclear semantics and is deprecated

title: Checks for simple __iter__ methods that return Generator, and for simple __aiter__ methods that return AsyncGenerator.
summary: Using (Async)Iterator for these methods is simpler and more elegant. More importantly, it also reflects the fact that the precise kind of iterator returned from an __iter__ method is usually an implementation detail that could change at any time. Type annotations help define a contract for a function; implementation details should not leak into that contract. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Use `{}` as the return value for simple `{}` methods

title: Checks for classes inheriting from typing.Generic[] where Generic[] is not the last base class in the bases tuple.
summary: If Generic[] is not the final class in the bases tuple, unexpected behaviour can occur at runtime (See this CPython issue for an example). Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.13.0.
message_templates: `Generic[]` should always be the last base class

title: Checks for redundant LiteralNone annotations.
summary: While LiteralNone is a valid type annotation, it is semantically equivalent to None. Prefer None over LiteralNone for both consistency and readability. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.13.0.
message_templates: Use `None` rather than `Literal[None]`
Use `Optional[Literal[...]]` rather than `Literal[None, ...]`
Use `Literal[...] | None` rather than `Literal[None, ...]`

title: Checks for duplicate members in a typing.Literal[] slice.
summary: Duplicate literal members are redundant and should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.6.0.
message_templates: Duplicate literal member `{}`

title: Checks for the presence of PEP 484-style positional-only parameters.
summary: Historically, PEP 484 recommended prefixing parameter names with double underscores (__) to indicate to a type checker that they were positional-only. However, PEP 570 (introduced in Python 3.8) introduced dedicated syntax for positional-only arguments. If a forward slash (/) is present in a function signature on Python 3.8+, all parameters prior to the slash are interpreted as positional-only. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Use PEP 570 syntax for positional-only parameters

title: Checks for redundant FinalLiteral[...] annotations.
summary: All constant variables annotated as Final are understood as implicitly having Literal types by a type checker. As such, a FinalLiteral[...] annotation can often be replaced with a bare Final, annotation, which will have the same meaning to the type checker while being more concise and more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: `Final[Literal[{}]]` can be replaced with a bare `Final`

title: Checks for code that branches on sys.version_info comparisons where branches corresponding to older Python versions come before branches corresponding to newer Python versions.
summary: As a convention, branches that correspond to newer Python versions should come first. This makes it easier to understand the desired behavior, which typically corresponds to the latest Python versions. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pyi and made it stable in 0.8.0.
message_templates: Put branches for newer Python versions first when branching on `sys.version_info` comparisons
